title: Leg1/Leg2 staleness guard is count-equality only: equal-count membership drift between gather and broadcast slips the guard, strands the unlisted staker in a terminally-migrating pool, and the script is not re-runnable (initiateMigration is one-shot)
location: SkimAndLeg1Migration.s.sol:146-157 (count-only check), :269-278 (post-assert); lib/stable-staker/src/StableStaker.sol:425 (initiateMigration one-way). Leg2 instance: Leg2Migration.s.sol:126-136 (count-only require).
description: The preflight compares only .count against live stakerCount. If one staker exits and another enters between the gather snapshot and the broadcast (counts equal, membership different), preflight passes; the batch then processes the stale list — the departed address yields amount 0 (skipped) and the new staker is never migrated. The post-assert stakerCount==0 catches it, but in broadcast mode (--skip-simulation --slow) it fires only AFTER all on-chain txs have landed: the pool is then in terminal Migrating state with one stranded staker, and re-running reverts at initiateMigration. Recovery is possible but undocumented (permissionless userMigrate, or manual migrator.migrate(token,[missed])). The same count-only weakness exists on the leg2 entry against the temp staker; the leg2 exposure is narrower because temp is a short-lived transit contract most users never touch directly, and the post-assert there also fails loud.
impact: Operational footgun: a benign user action in the gather->broadcast window can leave the migration half-finished on mainnet with no scripted recovery path. No funds lost (userMigrate exists); availability/runbook risk only. Probability low at the current 3/6-staker population.

classification.assetImpact: No funds lost (permissionless userMigrate exists as recovery). A benign user join/exit in the gather->broadcast window can leave one staker unmigrated and the pool in terminal Migrating with no scripted recovery path.
attackPath: 1. Count-only preflight passes when one staker exits and another enters (counts equal, membership differs).
2. Batch processes the stale list; departed address yields 0, new staker never migrated.
3. In --skip-simulation broadcast the post-assert fires only after txs land, leaving terminal Migrating; re-run reverts at one-shot initiateMigration.
classification.likelihood: Low — requires a benign user action in a narrow window at the current 3/6-staker population; not fork-demonstrated, analysis-supported.
classification.assumptions: Recovery via permissionless userMigrate or manual migrator.migrate is possible but undocumented.
classification.externalRequirements: User action in the gather->broadcast window.

evidence: Code reading of preflight + StableStaker terminal-migration semantics; story-055 ResumeStableStakerMigration as prior drift evidence (closure manifest cluster note). Not fork-demonstrated (would require staged user txs); analysis-supported. Leg2 instance: Leg2Migration.s.sol:126-136; stake/withdraw permitted while Active.
recommendation: Strengthen the guard: have gather store keccak256 of the sorted staker list and have preflight recompute it from getStakers() on-chain; or migrate from a fresh on-chain getStakers() read inside the script instead of a JSON snapshot (counts are tiny). For leg2, optionally freeze the transit temp staker before gather. Document the gather->broadcast no-new-stakes window and the userMigrate/manual-batch recovery in the runbook.
dedupNotes: COLLAPSED leg1 idx3 (canonical, WeakDriftGuard) and leg2 idx3 (CountOnlyStalenessGuard, same root cause against the transit temp staker). One root-cause family (count-only staleness guard / snapshot-vs-broadcast drift). Canonical entryPoint = migrate:ys-swap-leg1. Both Low; the leg2 instance is narrower and folded as a cross-entry-point instance rather than a separate finding.
sanitizationReason: New entry point migrate:ys-swap-leg1. Count-only staleness guard / membership-drift footgun. Non-obvious operator footgun (Law-3 in-scope), not obvious admin misconfig. Distinct from ledger. NEW.
severityJustification: Operational footgun (weak count-only staleness guard) with low likelihood at current scale and a recovery path (userMigrate) that prevents fund loss, so Low. The hazard is availability/runbook risk — a half-finished mainnet migration with no scripted recovery — which is a non-obvious owner footgun worth surfacing with safe-config guidance but does not meet the Medium value-leak/availability-impact bar.
